leftEvidence.title: A blind man calls the Son of David near Jericho

points.label: Action and response
points.left: A blind man asks what the passing crowd means, hears Jesus of Nazareth, cries to the Son of David, persists through rebuke, receives sight, follows, and leads public praise.
points.right: Jesus asks how the Christ is David’s son, cites David’s psalm about the Lord at God’s right hand, and repeats the unresolved relation.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places Davidic address moves from heard identity to restored sight and communal praise inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places Davidic descent and lordship remain in deliberate tension inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: Luke 18:35–43 and Luke 20:41–44 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Gospel and Apostolic Memory” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Luke asks how David’s Lord is also his son

payload.tension: Luke 18:35–43 foregrounds Davidic address moves from heard identity to restored sight and communal praise; Luke 20:41–44 foregrounds Davidic descent and lordship remain in deliberate tension. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
